evidence.reason: The shown journal guard at line 755 runs only after the runbook has acquired the hold, stopped triggers, drained services, and drained the queue. An unresolved controller transaction therefore does not prevent the initial service disruption, and a drain that hangs or fails can prevent the guard from running at all. Moving the check before Hold.acquire() preserves the clear-journal path while making the existing refusal effective; this is an ordinary ordering defect, not a new protection requirement.
